# creditor <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="creditor hex logo: two parrots on a wire saying the same thing" />

```{=markdown}
<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/rundel/creditor/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rundel/creditor/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->
```

Exploratory R bindings to [Loro](https://loro.dev), a Rust library of conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs). Replicas of a document edit independently, exchange updates as raw vectors, and converge to the same contents. Text (including rich text marks and cursors), map, list, movable list, counter, and tree containers are supported, and they can be nested. Documents keep their full history, which can be listed, compared, checked out, and reverted. Exports can be full or shallow snapshots, incremental updates, or JSON. Subscriptions report changes as they are committed, an undo manager reverses local edits, and an ephemeral store shares presence state such as cursors.

See `vignette("containers", package = "creditor")` for a tour of each container type and how it merges concurrent edits.

## Installation

Building from source needs a Rust toolchain: cargo and `rustc >= 1.85`.

```{r}
#| eval: false
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("rundel/creditor")
```

## Example

Editing functions return the document or container they were given, so edits chain with the pipe.

Two replicas edit the same text concurrently and then merge.

```{r}
library(creditor)

a = loro_doc() |>                    # replica `a` starts the text
  text_insert(1, "Hello")
b = loro_doc() |>                    # replica `b` starts from a snapshot of `a`
  doc_import(doc_export(a))

text_push(a, " world")               # concurrent edits, not yet synced
text_insert(b, 1, ">> ")

doc_merge(b, a) |>                   # each replica merges the changes it is missing
  text_get()

doc_merge(a, b) |>
  text_get()
```

`doc_merge()` is for replicas in the same R session. Replicas in different processes send each other raw vectors instead: `doc_export_updates(a, from = version)` holds the changes made to `a` since a version the other replica reported with `doc_version()`, and `doc_import()` applies them.

Containers nest: a map or list can hold plain values or child containers, each of which merges independently. New containers are made with `loro_text()`, `loro_list()`, `loro_map()`, and friends, and stored like any other value.

```{r}
doc = loro_doc()

note = doc_map(doc, "note") |>
  map_set(
    title = "Groceries",                   # plain value, replaced whole
    items = loro_list("milk", "eggs"),     # child containers merge their contents
    body = loro_text("Buy before Friday")
  )

list_push(note$items, "bread")             # edit a child container in place

doc |>
  doc_value() |>
  str()
```

The title is stored as a plain value: it changes only by being set again, so when two replicas set it concurrently one of the values wins. The items and body are containers, with handles (`note$items`, `note$body`) that the `list_*` and `text_*` functions edit in place, and concurrent edits to them from different replicas are all kept. The same goes for R lists: `list("milk", "eggs")` would store a plain value that comes back as an ordinary R list, which `list_push()` cannot extend. Use plain values for things that change as a whole and containers for things people edit piece by piece.

Text can carry marks, and a cursor keeps pointing at the same character as the text changes.

```{r}
doc = loro_doc() |>
  text_insert(1, "Hello world") |>
  text_mark(1, 5, bold = TRUE)             # "Hello" is bold

cursor = text_cursor(doc, 7)               # at the "w" of "world"

doc |>
  text_update("Hello brave new world") |>  # applies only the differences
  text_delta() |>                          # runs of text with their marks
  str()

cursor_pos(doc, cursor)                    # still at the "w", now character 17
```

Every version stays reachable.

```{r}
doc = loro_doc(peer_id = 1) |>
  text_insert(1, "Hello") |>
  doc_commit("greeting") |>                # label each commit with a message
  text_push(" world") |>
  doc_commit("audience")

(changes = doc_changes(doc))               # one row per change

doc |>
  doc_fork(at = "greeting") |>             # a copy at the "greeting" version
  text_get()
```

Subscriptions make live sync a one-liner, and undo reverses only local edits.

```{r}
a = loro_doc()
b = loro_doc()

sync = doc_subscribe_local_updates(a, \(bytes) doc_import(b, bytes))  # send `a`'s updates to `b`
manager = doc_undo_manager(a)              # track `a`'s local edits

a |>
  text_insert(1, "Hello") |>
  doc_commit()                             # delivers the update to `b`
text_get(b)

undo(manager)                              # undo is an edit too, so it syncs
text_get(b)

unsubscribe(sync)                          # stop syncing
```

## Shiny example

An example app shows two replicas of one document side by side. Each pane can be taken offline to make concurrent edits, which merge when it comes back online. Below the panes a timeline shows every edit as a bubble, in one row per replica above an axis of edit times; hovering a bubble shows what was changed and by whom, and selecting one shows the text at that point with the edit's insertions and deletions highlighted.

```{r}
#| eval: false
shiny::runApp(system.file("examples/sync-editors", package = "creditor"))
```
